design_models.name: BoltzGen

design_models.blurb: Designs directly in 3D around a target structure you provide (PDB/mmCIF plus a contig saying what stays fixed vs. what is designed): binders, motif scaffolds, DNA/RNA binders. Designs come back ordered on whether the output has the chains the contig asked for and how well the kept motif survived, which is a structural order and not a confidence one; refold designs with a Fold job to score them. Designed positions are named by the model's own sequence head, so each design comes back with a sequence. Treat it as a starting point: upstream recommends redesigning it with a tool like ProteinMPNN before ordering. One size caveat: on the target walked to the 1024 ceiling, designs at 768 and 832 total residues came back with a break in the designed backbone, where 640, 704 and 896-1024 did not, so check the designed chain is continuous before using a design in that range.
design_models.name: RFdiffusion3

params.help: Independent designs for the same spec (each its own noise draw; batched on-device).

design_models.blurb: Generates binder backbones against a target structure, conditioned on a distogram of the target. Fast, and the output is a backbone only: no sequence, no ranking, no confidence score. Take the coordinates to a sequence-design tool before ordering anything. For a ranked, sequenced binder use BoltzGen.
design_models.name: PXDesign

params.help: Independent designs for the same target (one batched diffusion trajectory).
params.label: Designs to generate

params.help: Sampling steps per design. 400 (the upstream default) gives the cleanest backbones; fewer is faster.
params.label: Diffusion steps

params.help: Noise seed. The same seed and target give the same designs.
params.label: Seed

design_models.blurb: Designs all-atom proteins around a target structure you provide (mmCIF plus a contig saying what stays fixed and what is designed): binders, motif scaffolds, antibody and nanobody CDR loops. Every design is made against a target, so the contig always keeps something. A trunk integrates a flow in an autoencoder's latent space and the decoder writes coordinates and a sequence in one step, so each design comes back with a sequence. Designs come back ordered on the kept motif and the chain count, which is a structural order and not a confidence one; refold designs with a Fold job to score them. How much thinking a design gets is a knob (the recipe), not a fixed cost.
design_models.name: RFD4-Proteina

params.help: Independent designs for the same spec. Each gets its own seed, batched on the card at small sizes and spread across the fleet above them.
params.label: Designs to generate

params.help: How many trunk passes a design spends and where: 120 for the low family, 180 for the released thinking_medium, 300 for thinking_high. More passes cost proportionally more. Upstream uses medium/front_loaded for binders, high/front_loaded for antibody and nanobody CDRs, medium/midpeak for enzymes and motif scaffolds.
params.label: Thinking budget

params.help: Flow-matching steps per design. 60 is what every recipe is built for; fewer is a different, worse model rather than a faster one.
params.label: Integration steps

params.help: Noise seed. The same seed and spec give the same designs. A contig with a variable-length segment draws that length from the seed too.
params.label: Seed

models.blurb: Folds protein, DNA, RNA and ligand complexes and predicts binding affinity. Uses a multiple-sequence alignment (MSA) for best accuracy. The most capable model: choose it when in doubt, or whenever you need ligands, nucleic acids, affinity or constraints.
models.name: Boltz-2

models.blurb: Language-model folding, no MSA required, though it will use one if supplied for extra accuracy. Co-folds protein, DNA, RNA and ligand chains; it predicts no binding affinity. A quick, lightweight choice for a protein structure or a small cocrystal.
models.label: Standard
models.name: ESMFold-2

models.blurb: ESMFold-2 tuned for maximum throughput: always single-sequence, and it co-folds ligands and nucleic acids like the standard checkpoint. Accuracy is typically very close to ESMFold-2, and it is the model to reach for when screening thousands of sequences at once.
models.label: Fast
models.name: ESMFold-2 Fast

models.blurb: The OpenFold Consortium's open AlphaFold3 reproduction, running fully on-device. Folds multi-chain complexes of proteins, RNA and DNA using a multiple-sequence alignment by default (turn it off to fold single-sequence). No ligands and no affinity: for ligands on this same stack use OpenBind-0, for affinity Boltz-2. The published weights are a preview checkpoint trained to 155k steps, well short of the full AlphaFold3 schedule, so read the confidence scores before trusting a prediction.
models.name: OpenFold3
models.tagline: The OpenFold consortium's AlphaFold3, preview weights.

models.blurb: The OpenFold Consortium's OpenBind-0 checkpoint on the OpenFold3 architecture, running fully on-device. Unlike the OpenFold3 preview weights it co-folds small-molecule ligands alongside proteins, RNA and DNA, using a multiple-sequence alignment by default. It predicts structure and confidence, not binding affinity. For affinity use Boltz-2.
models.name: OpenBind-0
models.tagline: OpenFold3 stack, tuned for protein-ligand co-folding.

models.blurb: The Baker lab's RoseTTAFold3, running fully on-device. Folds multi-chain complexes of proteins, RNA, DNA and small-molecule ligands, using a multiple-sequence alignment by default (turn it off to fold single-sequence). Structure only: no binding affinity, and no covalent modifications or binding constraints from this input format. For those use Boltz-2.
models.name: RoseTTAFold3

models.blurb: OpenDDE with its general protein-complex checkpoint. Co-folds multi-chain protein complexes on the Protenix-v2 stack plus a structural-token expander, using an MSA by default. Protein-only (no ligands, nucleic acids or affinity). For binding affinity, use Boltz-2; for ligands or DNA/RNA, use Boltz-2.
models.label: General
models.name: OpenDDE · General

models.blurb: OpenDDE with its antibody-antigen checkpoint selected. Co-folds an antibody (Fab heavy/light) with its antigen on the Protenix-v2 stack, using an MSA by default. Protein-only, no affinity. Accuracy is verified to match the reference OpenDDE implementation: strong on standard antibody-antigen complexes, and it shares the reference's own limitation on some hard targets (a checkpoint characteristic, not a port defect), so don't expect uniformly high accuracy on every antibody-antigen input.
models.label: Antibody-Antigen
models.name: OpenDDE · Antibody-Antigen

models.blurb: AlphaFold2 initial-guess, the filter a binder-design pipeline uses to tell a real design from a plausible one. Give it a design you already have, meaning a structure carrying the target chain and the binder backbone plus the binder's sequence. It re-predicts the complex from those coordinates and reports ipTM and interface pAE for the interface. Paste it as `target:` (with the structure inline) and `binder:`; a chain list is a different input and it is refused. No alignment and no sampling: the same input gives the same answer. It runs Google DeepMind's AlphaFold2 parameters (params_model_1_ptm, 2022-12-06 release), licensed under CC BY 4.0.
models.name: AF2-IG
models.tagline: Scores a binder you already designed.

models.blurb: Mol-1, model by Molence. Predicts the 3D structure of complexes of proteins, DNA, RNA and small molecules (CCD codes or SMILES). It is derived from Protenix with a wider pair track and runs fully on-device. Uses a multiple-sequence alignment by default (turn it off to fold single-sequence). Reports pLDDT, pTM, ipTM and PAE. For binding affinity, use Boltz-2.

typical_cost_note: typical_cost is history from the last 7 days, not a quote. A prediction runs each target (input structure) on its own chip and is billed per chip-second, so multiply usd_per_target_p90 by the targets you submit for what most jobs that size cost (usd_per_target_p50 for a median one). usd_p50 and usd_p90 are per job and follow whatever batch sizes users sent that week (targets_p50). A design or embedding job splits its own work across chips, so it has only the per-job figures. null means fewer than 20 jobs.
